paragraphs: One-sentence assessment | This career is worth exploring further only if you are willing to spend extended periods serving customers on the branch front line, get account-opening documents and identity verification right the first time, and maintain reviewable records that meet regulatory requirements despite customer pressure and performance targets.

Core output | Connect customer identity and account-opening verification results, explanations of account and product terms, system entries and archived records into a traceable account-opening file: registration, risk disclosures, customer confirmations and follow-up, beyond merely completing a data entry.

20—120-minute safe trial | Conduct a simulated exercise with fictional customer information: list identity documents and supporting materials needed to open an individual account, write three questions that must clarify the customer's intent or purpose, and prepare an explanation of how to defer processing when information is incomplete. Do not use this exercise to open an account for a real customer or reach compliance conclusions.

First hurdle | Verify authorization boundaries first: who may verify identity, approve account opening and handle suspicious circumstances. Covered US institutions must verify customer identity, identify beneficial owners of legal entity customers and conduct ongoing monitoring under FinCEN customer due diligence rules. In mainland China, individual bank settlement accounts must be opened under real names using personal identity documents, with identity verified; organizational accounts are subject to approval or filing depending on their category. Specific authorization and escalation routes follow institutional policies.

entries: Account-opening interviews and identity verification | Interview customers to obtain required account-opening information, verify identity document validity, consistency between the document and applicant, and intent to open the account; request supporting documentation when necessary.
Document organization and system entry | Compile new account information, enter account information into computer systems, and file relevant forms and documents.
Service and product explanations | Answer customer questions and explain services and application procedures for deposit accounts, bank cards, certificates of deposit and direct deposit.
Counter transactions and payments | Perform teller duties as needed, receive and record customer deposits and fees, issue receipts and execute fund transfers.
Error investigation and correction | Investigate and correct errors at customers' requests using customer and bank records.
Referrals and collaboration | Refer customers to the appropriate personnel when their needs extend beyond account services, and report abnormalities under institutional procedures.

paragraphs: The core capability of new accounts clerks is implementing compliance requirements at the account-opening counter while explaining them clearly to customers: systematically checking identities and documents, entering and filing information through standard procedures, explaining terms and fees in understandable language, and knowing when to defer processing and escalate incomplete information or abnormal signals.

Work primarily takes place at branch counters and customer waiting areas, almost entirely indoors. O*NET work context data show that 79% work indoors in controlled conditions daily, 90% use the telephone daily, 87% use email daily, 79% have face-to-face discussions daily, and 89% maintain constant contact with others.

Accuracy and repetition requirements are high: 67% consider exactness or accuracy extremely important and 74% consider repeating the same tasks extremely important; 27% report extremely serious consequences of errors and 11% very serious consequences. Meanwhile, 89% work 40 hours per week, and 100% have regular schedules.

The emphasis is on combining process discipline with communication: getting account-opening documents right the first time, making terms understandable, and completing verification and records as required by regulators despite performance targets and time pressure.

Quality is measured by documents and identity verification passing the first time, traceable entries and filing, confirmation records for explanations of terms and fees, and abnormalities escalated and resolved under procedures, rather than account-opening volume alone.

Responsibility boundaries | Responsibility for account approval, identity verification conclusions and judgments on suspicious circumstances rests with institutional policies and authorization chains. Counter staff must not independently relax identity checks, skip due diligence steps or promise approval outcomes. In mainland China, financial institutions legally bear account-opening and anti-money laundering obligations; specific operations follow current institutional policies and the latest regulatory documents.

The workflow proceeds as follows: reception and needs identification → verify identity and documents → explain terms and fees and obtain confirmation → enter and file information → process payments or make referrals → escalate abnormalities and follow up. Occupational boundaries | This occupation is distinct from credit approval staff, financial advisers and anti-money laundering specialists. Loan approval, investment advice and classification of suspicious transactions are outside counter staff's independent decision-making scope.

Tellers | Primarily handle cash and check receipts and payments and account transactions, with fewer account-opening interviews and product explanations. This occupation centers on document verification, explanations of terms and account entry during account opening, with counter payments handled as needed.

Customer service representatives | Focus on inquiries, complaints and product guidance, without operational responsibility for account opening and identity verification. Credit and financial advisers handle loan approval recommendations and investment product allocation; this occupation only identifies needs and makes referrals.

Selection signal | Compare more than the fact that these roles all work in bank branches. Consider who handles identity verification and account-opening operations, who makes approval or investment recommendations, and who decides to defer processing or report suspicious circumstances.
Centers on cash and check receipts and payments and account transactions, typically without responsibility for judging the completeness of account-opening documents or customer due diligence.

Consider teller work if you prefer standardized transactions, cash management and counter service. Consider customer service representative work if you prefer identifying needs and explaining products without operational responsibility for account opening.

Start with tasks | Task exposure to generative AI does not equal actual adoption, the probability of automation or job disappearance. This page analyzes tasks and work contexts from O*NET 43-4141.00 individually and does not invent a replacement rate or score for this occupation.
More suitable for assistance | Customer document checklist verification, account-opening form field checks, drafts explaining terms and fees, organization of FAQ scripts and follow-up reminders.

Information retrieval assistance | May help locate current institutional account-opening requirements and product description versions. Humans must review cited terms, effective dates and applicable scope.
Risk-screening assistance | May flag missing or inconsistent information, but cannot replace identity verification, verification of intent to open an account or judgments on suspicious circumstances.

Responsibility cannot be delegated to general-purpose models: intent to open an account, acceptance of documents, approval or deferral, judgments on suspicious circumstances and customer commitments follow institutional authorization. Compliant digital verification may assist; this does not require every step to be entirely manual or grant general-purpose models authority to process accounts.

Verify valid identity information, intent to open an account and lawful agency relationships according to the channel and applicable rules. Review and document abnormalities through the authorization chain; do not generalize that every account opening requires personal attendance.

Data requirements | Process customer identity and account information only in institution-authorized systems. Do not enter identity document images, account materials or customer information into unauthorized external tools.

Capability development | Build skills in identity verification and document review, explaining terms and handling objections, accurate system operation, and identifying and escalating abnormalities, beyond faster data entry.

This is the US O*NET43-4141.00 account-opening service occupation. This review did not verify a one-to-one Chinese classification mapping. Chinese accounts are divided into organizational and individual accounts; verify individual real-name requirements and intent to open an account under applicable rules. China's 2019 reform removed enterprise bank account licensing: basic and temporary deposit accounts of domestic corporate legal entities, unincorporated enterprises and individually owned businesses moved from approval to filing. Government bodies, public institutions and other organizations follow applicable rules; do not claim that licensing was removed for all organizational accounts.

This National Bureau of Statistics industry table does not list new accounts clerks separately. Financial industry averages serve only as a reference for related financial institution employers. This review did not obtain an occupational wage distribution on a comparable basis.

Coverage includes legal entities in urban areas with 5 or more employees; individually owned businesses and freelancers are excluded.

Insufficient evidence: this review did not obtain nationwide Chinese occupational wages on a comparable basis. Industry averages do not support estimates for individuals or percentiles. Verify valid identity documents, intent to open an account and lawful agency relationships. Financial institutions bear due diligence, retention and reporting obligations; counter staff follow the current allocation of authorized responsibilities.

The 2025 BLS OEWS data displayed by O*NET report the exact occupation 43-4141.00: median hourly wage of USD 22.92 and median annual wage of USD 47,670. These figures are not starting salaries or individual quoted rates.

National annual wage percentiles under the same definition are USD 38,180 at the 10th percentile, USD 43,920 at the 25th, USD 55,100 at the 75th and USD 60,910 at the 90th. Corresponding hourly wages are USD 18.36, 21.12, 26.49 and 29.29.
The percentiles and medians all use 2025 BLS OEWS national data and cannot be directly compared across years, regions or institution types.

OEWS includes sales commissions, incentive pay and production bonuses, while excluding attendance bonuses, nonproduction bonuses and overtime premiums, among other items. Performance bonuses cannot all be treated as excluded. Employee wages exclude self-employment and partnership income and are not take-home pay.
Lower percentiles are not starting salaries for newcomers, and distribution data cannot be used to estimate individual take-home pay or after-tax income.

Scheduling, performance pay and commission structures at community banks, large bank branches, credit unions and telephone service centers affect actual income. Verify the specific institution, region and job level. US figures cannot be converted into individual income in mainland China.

Verification method | Personality and interest labels cannot determine fit. Use fictional customer information to practice identity verification and document checklists, and obtain evaluation from experienced branch personnel in a compliant teaching or supervised training setting.

Scope statement | This checklist cannot replace institutional account-opening policies, anti-money laundering procedures, identity verification or consumer protection requirements. Main risks include inadequate identity verification or document review, unverified account-opening intent, procedural shortcuts to meet targets, mishandling customer information and identity document images, and failure to escalate abnormalities promptly. Controls should be tailored to the institution and jurisdiction.

Identity, document, intent, abnormal-signal and confidentiality risks must be handled under institutional procedures. Lawful agency does not imply suspicion. Two-person review and spot checks are risk-tailored editorial recommendations, without claims that they are universally mandatory or that their effectiveness has been verified.

O*NET's 67% accuracy requirement and 27% extremely serious error consequences support the work context, not risk incidence. US FinCEN CDD must be read alongside 2026-R001; beneficial owners do not have to be reverified for every new account. China's enterprise licensing reform and anti-money laundering due diligence apply according to entity type. Controls are editorial recommendations; relevant departments and personnel retain legal / authorized responsibilities.

Account-opening frontline staff, supervisors and compliance and anti-money laundering personnel may all be affected. This review has no comparative evidence that less-experienced personnel face the highest risk and does not rank groups.

Possible consequences | Identity or document errors may cause account-opening failures, harm customer funds and rights, and result in regulatory penalties. Unidentified abnormal account openings may facilitate money laundering, telecommunications and online fraud or other illegal activities. Mishandling customer information creates data compliance and reputational risks.

career_path_block.direct_answer: First verify the work jurisdiction, institutional hiring requirements and authorization. US BLS43-4141 lists high school and moderate-term on-the-job training as typical; O*NET education survey values of 46/28/15 are not Chinese standards. No certification search results do not establish absence of licensing requirements in all jurisdictions. Institutions verify product, system and compliance training and clearance. China's 2019 reform removed enterprise bank account licensing: basic and temporary deposit accounts of domestic corporate legal entities, unincorporated enterprises and individually owned businesses moved from approval to filing. Government bodies, public institutions and other organizations follow applicable rules; do not claim that licensing was removed for all organizational accounts.

locale_requirements.credential_boundary: Education, internal institutional authorization, product and compliance training, system permissions and regulatory requirements are distinct statuses. description.text: New accounts clerks (O*NET 43-4141.00) interview customers at banks and other depository financial institutions, verify identity documents and materials, explain account services, enter account information and file records, and handle counter payments and error correction as needed. This page explains their tasks, preparation requirements, compliance boundaries, and Chinese and US wage and employment definitions.

subject.name: New accounts clerks
subject.summary: New accounts clerks (O*NET-SOC 43-4141.00) handle account-opening stages at banks and other depository financial institutions: interviewing customers, verifying identity documents and materials, explaining account and service terms, entering account information into systems and filing records, handling counter payments, transfers and error correction as needed, and escalating abnormalities in customer identity or transactions under institutional procedures. This page uses only official sources to explain occupational scope, tasks, preparation requirements, Chinese and US statistical definitions, and authorization boundaries.
